name: pterm-per-call-text-rendering-environments
instr:
Give every pterm text printer a reusable per-call rendering context so concurrent destinations can choose independent writers, widths, styling, and color capabilities without mutating package globals. Contextual printing must also expose the writer's actual outcome while preserving each printer's established rendering and terminal side effects.

A zero-value `TextContext` makes every `ContextTextPrinter` behave byte-for-byte like its existing operations under current globals, including ordinary `SectionPrinter` styling and padding. Explicit context choices are immutable call-local overrides, isolated from concurrent contexts, global changes, and subsequent ordinary calls. Across `BasicTextPrinter`, `BoxPrinter`, `CenterPrinter`, `HeaderPrinter`, `ParagraphPrinter`, `PrefixPrinter`, `SectionPrinter`, `Color`, `RGB`, and `RGBStyle`, every contextual operation is its corresponding established operation evaluated entirely under the resolved context, preserving all printer-specific argument interpretation, formatting, layout, suppression, reset, Unicode, and terminal side-effect semantics. This equivalence includes `SprintContext` and `SprintfContext` argument handling, line-wise styling, box and header geometry, and every prefix mode and annotation. Positive width controls all wrapping, centering, and full-width geometry without splitting overlong words or producing negative padding; `WithTextStyling(TextModeRaw)` alone bypasses paragraph wrapping.
